ECE 685 | Power Systems Design L05
Single-Phase AC Circuits I
From a time waveform to an RMS phasor and back
Buxin She
Mike Wiegers Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

Lecture outline
1 read amplitude, frequency, period, and phase from a cosine waveform
2 convert peak values to RMS values and explain what RMS means
3 convert among time-domain, polar, and rectangular forms, and
4 choose the right form, validate compatibility, and check a phasor sum.
A phasor is compact when frequency and the RMS convention are declared first.

ECE 685 | Single-Phase AC I 33/34

Phasor summary
Knowledge to carry forward
Representation: one waveform;
one phasor in polar or rectangular
coordinates.
Magnitude: waveform coefficients
are peak values; phasor
magnitudes are RMS values.
Conversion: use cosine and sine
for components; use magnitude and
atan2 for the inverse.
Compatibility: match 𝜔, physical
quantity and unit, convention, and
angle reference.
Operation: add or subtract in
rectangular form; multiply or divide
in polar form.
Check and reconstruct: verify
signs and reverse conversion; then
restore peak, 𝜔, phase, and unit.
Declare conventions, convert, choose the form, compute, check, and reconstruct.
